name: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
problem: Frontier-scale MoE LLMs cost a great deal to train and to serve, and the two usual levers - more expert parallelism, more fine-grained routing - make training stability and inference communication harder.
mechanism: A 671B-total / 37B-activated MoE trained on 14.8T tokens. (1) MLA from DeepSeek-V2 for the KV cache. (2) DeepSeekMoE with auxiliary-loss-free load balancing (a bias term per expert, rather than an auxiliary loss) plus a shared-expert route that is always on. (3) Multi-token prediction. (4) FP8 mixed-precision training across almost every matmul, with per-tensor and per-block scaling to preserve stability. (5) Dual-pipeline parallelism to overlap host-device communication with computation.
speedup_reported: NOT AN INFERENCE SPEEDUP. The paper's headline operational claim is training cost: full training of DeepSeek-V3 required 2.788M H800 GPU hours. The abstract's other claims are quality ('outperforms other open-source models, comparable to leading closed-source models') and stability ('no irrecoverable loss spikes, no rollbacks'). There is no serving throughput or latency figure in the abstract. The serving-relevant numbers for this architecture are in the deepseek-v2-mla record instead.
notes:
arXiv ID 2412.19437 verified via abs-page citation_title/citation_date on 2026-10-03; title matches. venue=arxiv-preprint: technical report, no venue claim in the arXiv comment, and an OpenReview search for the exact title returns no conference record. adoption=in-production rather than in-upstream-engine: this is the strongest adoption case in the batch - DeepSeek-V3 weights are released (github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, 104k stars, pushed 2025-08-28) and both major engines serve them, so the method is deployed in production systems, not merely present in an engine's model zoo. Explicitly noted so the record is not read as claiming MLA belongs to this paper - MLA is DeepSeek-V2's contribution and is recorded there; what this report adds is MLA-in-a-shipped-frontier-model plus the FP8 training recipe.
